rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic negator لن conveys the denier’s firm certainty that he will not return to life.
rows.anchor: الدال على تأكيد النفي وتأييده لحكاية جزمهم وقطعهم بنفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بلى cancels a negative assertion; it usually answers a negative question but can also follow a non-interrogative denial, as in 7:172 and 64:7.
rows.anchor: يجاب به الكلام المنفي لإبطال نفيه وأكثر وقوعه بعد الاستفهام عن النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here بلى begins a new sentence, as answer particles do.
rows.anchor: وموقع { بلى } الاستئناف كأحرف الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause explains بلى: the denier’s assumption is false because his Lord informed him through the Messenger that he will be resurrected.
rows.anchor: يعني أن ظنه باطل لأن ربه أنبأه بأنه يبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن reinforces the rebuttal of his denial of the resurrection taught by the Messenger; God knows his state while he does not, as 2:216 says.
rows.anchor: لرده إنكاره البعث الذي أخبر الله به على لسان رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بصيرا takes ب because intransitive بصر means to see someone clearly; the preposition conveys attachment or contact.
rows.anchor: فالباء فيه معناها الملابسة أو الإلصاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection enables recompense: God knows people’s deeds and their differing moral worth, so justice requires reward and punishment in an eternal life.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى حكمة البعث للجزاء لأن رب الناس عليم بأحوالهم فمنهم المصلح ومنهم المفسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sight here is a metaphor for complete knowledge of a person’s state.
rows.anchor: وأطلق البصر هنا على العلم التام بالشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the person who thought he would not return; God knows his circumstances, not merely his essence.
rows.anchor: والمراد : العلم بأحواله لا بذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preposing به emphasizes that God certainly knows him and also serves the verse endings.
rows.anchor: أي بصير به لا محالة مع مراعاة الفواصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath and its answer in 84:16–19 follow the detailed account through 84:7, condensing the reckoning and recompense and summing up the terrors ahead.
rows.anchor: فكان هذا التفريع فذلكة وحوصلة لما فصل من الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of يؤمنون is omitted but supplied by context: resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: يؤمنون } محذوف يدل عليه السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, يؤمنون is intransitive: they simply lack faith despite the evidence for God’s exclusive divinity, making their continued associationism astonishing.
rows.anchor: ويجوز تنزيل فعل { يؤمنون } منزلة اللازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse expresses astonishment and censure at their unbelief despite clear proofs of the message and warning.
rows.anchor: التعجيب والإنكار من عدم إيمانهم مع ظهور دلائل صدق ما دعوا إليه وأنذروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا يسجدون is coordinated with لا يؤمنون.
rows.anchor: لا يسجدون } عطف على { لا يؤمنون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The introductory time clause is fronted to emphasize and honor the Quran.
rows.anchor: ظرف قدم على عامله للاهتمام به وتنويه شأن القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting the Quran to them means recitation to convey the message and invite them to faith.
rows.anchor: وقراءة القرآن عليهم قراءته قراءة تبليغ ودعوة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول
rows.claim: Ibn Ubayy told the Prophet not to deceive or provoke them with Quran during their gatherings.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول : ( لا تغشنا به في مجالسنا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet recited Quran to al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, as Ibn Ashur discussed under Surat Abasa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن على الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sajdah means submission and humility: they do not submit to God, the Quran’s meanings, or its proof, nor believe its truth, as contrasted with their denial in 84:22.
rows.anchor: والسجود مستعمل بمعنى الخضوع والخشوع كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording does not establish a Quranic prostration at this verse.
rows.anchor: وليس في هذه الآية ما يقتضي أن عند هذه الآية سجدة من سجود القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur considers the stronger Maliki position to be that this is not one of the Quran’s prostration verses.
rows.anchor: الأصح من قول مالك وأصحابه أنها ليست من سجود القرآن خلافا لابن وهب

rows.speaker: ابن وهب
rows.claim: Ibn Wahb, a Maliki, counts fourteen Quranic prostrations, including this verse.
rows.anchor: خلافا لابن وهب من أصحاب مالك فإنه جعل سجودات القرآن أربع عشرة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi‘i holds that prostration here is recommended.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي : هي سنة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that prostration here is obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة : واجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur judges that eleven prostrations are established by sound reports from Companions.
rows.anchor: والأرجح أن عزائم السجود المسنونة إحدى عشرة سجدة وهي التي رويت بالأسانيد الصحيحة عن الصحابة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Reports say the Prophet prostrated at three additional verses including this one, but other reports conflict; Ibn Ashur allows that he left the prostration or did not emphasize it.
rows.anchor: ثلاث آيات غير الإحدى عشرة آية رويت فيها أخبار أنها سجد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عند قراءتها

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi identifies prostration at Surat al-Inshiqaq as the position of the Medinan Malikis.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن العربي السجود في سورة الانشقاق قول المدنيين من أصحاب مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to the preceding oath also warns polytheists that God knows their beliefs and deeds and will requite them.
rows.anchor: وقد تضمن هذا الجواب زيادة على إفادته تحقيق الجزاء إنذارا للمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to inspect the first creation follows from 86:4 and indirectly proves resurrection: a second creation is no harder than the first.
rows.anchor: الفاء لتفريع الأمر بالنظر في الخلقة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied argument is: if resurrection seems impossible, inspect your origin; this fāʾ makes the omitted premise understood.
rows.anchor: فالتقدير : فإن رأيتم البعث محالا فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نظر means intellectual reflection that leads to knowledge by inference; the command addresses deniers of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهو التفكر المؤدي إلى علم شيء بالاستدلال فالمأمور به نظر المنكر للبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من is an origin preposition governed by خلق; it is fronted with interrogative ما, asking what substance the human was created from.
rows.anchor: ابتدائية متعلقة ب { خلق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative ما makes نظر cease to take a direct object.
rows.anchor: استفهامية علقت فعل النظر العقلي عن العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question awakens people to necessary knowledge, comparable to asking what the human was created from in 80:18.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام مستعمل في الإيقاظ والتنبيه إلى ما يجب علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif of interrogative ما is omitted when it is governed by a preposition.
rows.anchor: وحذف ألف ( ما ) الاستفهامية على طريقة وقوعها مجرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this is not a genuine request for information, the speaker answers it with another question, as in 78:1–2.
rows.anchor: ولكون الاستفهام غير حقيقي أجاب عنه المتكلم بالاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الإنسان here means specifically the denier of resurrection, as the command’s connection shows.
rows.anchor: مراد به خصوص منكر البعث كما علمت آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دافق means issuing forcefully and swiftly; it most commonly describes a man’s semen.
rows.anchor: خارج بقوة وسرعة والأشهر أنه يقال على نطفة الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some linguists derive دافق as an active participle from intransitive دفق; most reject an intransitive use and treat it as passive.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور : لا يستعمل دفق قاصرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Where Qur’anic wording, syntax, semantics, or pause permits several readings without violating context, the passage should bear all of them.
rows.anchor: يجب حمل الكلام على جميعها كالوصل والوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One valid reading pauses after لا ريب or فيه; Ibn Ashur develops both effects in the next discussion.
rows.anchor: كالوصل والوقف في قوله تعالى ) لا ريب فيه هدى للمتقين (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same principle allows distinct pauses in 3:146 and 3:7, and either attachment of Ibrahim’s vocative to the reproach or threat in 19:46.
rows.anchor: باختلاف ارتباط النداء من قوله ( يا إبراهيم ) بالتوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Quran addresses every nation and age, God made it Arabic, which Ibn Ashur considers rich, concise, eloquent, flexible, and abundant in expression.
rows.anchor: وقد أراد الله تعالى أن يكون القرآن كتابا مخاطبا به كل الأمم في جميع العصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran packs many meanings Arabic syntax can bear into minimal wording, favoring concise expression and using forms rarer than in Arab eloquence.
rows.anchor: في أقل ما يسمح به نظم تلك اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the Quran’s subtle styles are simultaneous senses of a polysemous word, literal and figurative senses, explicit and allusive meanings, and implications carried by constructions.
rows.anchor: استعمال اللفظ المشترك في معنييه أو معانيه دفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rhetoricians recognized meanings implied by constructions, but simultaneous polysemy and literal-plus-figurative use remain disputed because prior Arabic usage rarely attested them.
rows.anchor: وبقي المبحثان الأولان وهما استعمال المشترك في معنييه أو معانيه

rows.speaker: الغزالي وأبو الحسين البصري
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali and Abu al-Husayn al-Basri allow a speaker to intend several senses of a shared word, but say this comes from intention rather than linguistic denotation.
rows.anchor: إذ قال الغزالي وأبو الحسين البصري يصح أن يراد بالمشترك عدة معان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur takes their point to mean that intended senses can be rational implications of a construction, requiring no metaphorical relation or cue.
rows.anchor: وظني بهما أنهما يريدان تصيير تلك الإرادة إلى أنها دلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur holds that a shared word can linguistically denote all or some of its several senses at once.
rows.anchor: والحق أن المشترك يصح إطلاقه على عدة من معانيه جميعا أو بعضا

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One group treats a shared word intended in multiple senses as literal; this is attributed to al-Shafi‘i, al-Baqillani, and most Mu‘tazilites.
rows.anchor: نسب إلى الشافعي وأبي بكر الباقلاني وجمهور المعتزلة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another group considers multiple intended senses figurative.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم : هو المجاز

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hajib reads al-Baqillani as allowing a shared word to carry multiple senses only with an indicator, which he takes to mark figurative usage.
rows.anchor: وجزم ابن الحاجب بأنه مراد الباقلاني من قوله في كتاب التقريب والإرشاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects Ibn al-Hajib’s reading: a metaphor cue blocks the literal sense, whereas every sense of a genuinely shared word is literal.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يستقيم لأن القرينة التي هي من علامات المجاز هي القرينة المانعة من إرادة المعنى الحقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cue for a shared word selects which literal senses, all or some, the speaker intends; treating these senses as nonliteral would erase the category.
rows.anchor: إذ معاني المشترك كلها من قبيل الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A brief pause can build anticipation like an explanatory ellipsis; the following clause then functions like a resumption, even if not formally one.
rows.anchor: السكوت عند كلمة وتعقيبها بما بعدها يجعل ما بعدها بمنزلة الاستئناف البياني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pausing after موسى in the question about his story creates anticipation; the following clause explains, while rhyme endings reinforce the pause.
rows.anchor: حصل البيان مع ما يحصل عند الوقف على كلمة موسى من قرينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stopping after لا ريب elides a completion such as no doubt that it is the Book; فيه هدى للمتقين begins a new sentence, conceding that it contains guidance even if opponents deny the whole is guidance.
rows.anchor: كان من قبيل إيجاز الحذف أي لا ريب في أنه الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Connecting فيه to the preceding clause is an elaborated reading in which what follows shows that the whole Book is guidance.
rows.anchor: وكان ما بعده مفيدا أن هذا الكتاب كله هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran generally varies wording and form instead of repeating them, except where repetition serves emphasis or another purpose.
rows.anchor: ومن أساليب القرآن العدول عن تكرير اللفظ والصيغة فيما عدا المقامات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In address to two women, the plural قلوب avoids repeating the dual form قلبا.
rows.anchor: فجاء بلفظ قلوب جمعا مع أن المخاطب امرأتان فلم يقل قلبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 6:139, خالصة follows the meaning of relative ما as feminine plural, while محرم follows its singular grammatical form.
rows.anchor: فروعي معنى ما الموصولة مرة فأتى بضمير جماعة المؤنث وهو خالصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When several formulations suit the context, the eloquent speaker may choose either or use both for variety; Quranic variation refreshes repeated material with a changed nuance and style.
rows.anchor: إن المقام قد يقتضي شيئين متساويين أو أشياء متساوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s eating is linked by و in 2:35 but by ف in 7:19; the village command varies between enter and dwell, with coordination and consequence both fitting.
rows.anchor: وقوله في الأعراف ) فكلا ( بفاء التفريع وكلاهما مطابق للمقام

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says the Quran varies between emphatic and more emphatic formulations, or good and better, rather than using the strongest form every time.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشاف في تفسير قوله تعالى ) إن ربي يعلم القول في السماء والأرض (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran broadened Arabic literary expression; before it, poetry was the dominant surviving and circulating form of Arab literature.
rows.anchor: ومنها اتساع أدب اللغة في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other Arab forms included sermons, proverbs, and dialogue: sermons were poorly retained and briefly influential, proverbs were concise lessons, and dialogue ranged from everyday talk to public assemblies.
rows.anchor: فأما الخطب فكانت تنسى بانتهاء المقامات المقولة فيها

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid’s verse depicts public assemblies with unknown visitors, expected benefits, and feared blame, illustrating the forum-dialogue genre Ibn Ashur describes.
rows.anchor: أشار إليها لبيد بقوله : وكثيرة غرباؤها مجهولة ترجى نوافلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sufi ishārāt are not alternate Quran interpretations: their authors say a verse suits an analogy or lesson, calling these signals rather than meanings, unlike esoteric Batini claims.
rows.anchor: فينبغي أن تعلموا أنهم ما كانوا يدعون أن كلامهم في ذلك تفسير للقرآن

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali accepts such allusions and reads the Prophetic report about angels not entering a house with a dog or image as an image of the heart: bad traits bar angelic light.
rows.anchor: فالغزالي يراها مقبولة ، قال في كتاب من الإحياء

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali says he is not replacing the report’s outward meaning; it only prompts reflection on inward states, unlike changing the apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: ولست أقول إن المراد من الحديث بلفظ البيت القلب وبالكلب الصفة المذمومة

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عطاء
rows.claim: A report in al-Bukhari’s Maghazi explains those who exchanged God’s favor for disbelief as Quraysh, identifies Muhammad as the favor, and takes the abode of ruin as Badr.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن عطاء في قوله تعالى ) ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمة الله كفرا (

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi rejects all Sufi allusions and denies that the Quran has an inward layer beyond its outward meaning.
rows.anchor: وابن العربي في كتاب العواصم يرى إبطال هذه الإشارات كلها

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi praises al-Ghazali’s fight against esoterics and philosophers but says his involvement with Sufism made him depart from the truth.
rows.anchor: بعد ما نوه بالثناء على الغزالي في تصديه للرد على الباطنية والفلاسفة قال : وقد كان أبو حامد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur classifies the signals into three kinds: analogy, associative wordplay, and moral lessons drawn from any experience, including Quranic admonitions.
rows.anchor: وعندي إن هذه الإشارات لا تعدو واحدا من ثلاثة أنحاء : الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an analogy, mosques can stand for hearts that submit through knowledge of God; blocking remembrance suggests blocking divine knowledge, and ruining them suggests clouding them with partisanship and passion.
rows.anchor: ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه أنه إشارة للقلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second kind is auditory association: a listener turns the sound of من ذا into من ذل and makes it a lesson about humility and nearness, following the listener’s concern.
rows.anchor: وهذا كمن قال في قوله تعالى ) من ذا الذي يشفع (

rows.speaker: محي الدين
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi calls this sound-association سماعا; Ibn Ashur considers that description ingenious.
rows.anchor: ورأيت الشيخ محي الدين يسمي هذا النوع سماعا ولقد أبدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third kind is moral exhortation: readers may infer that a heart disobeying the messenger of higher knowledge will meet calamity, without claiming this is exegesis.
rows.anchor: فإذا أخذوا من قوله تعالى ) فعصى فرعون الرسول فأخذناه أخذا وبيلا (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur recounts a Sufi who wept after hearing that an unfruitful branch was fit only for fire, applying the remark to an unfruitful heart.
rows.anchor: ومن حكاياتهم في غير باب التفسير أن بعضهم مر برجل يقول لآخر : هذا العود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a geminated verb is intransitive, its form usually signals abundance or intensification; the Shafiya states this rule, though abundance can be figurative.
rows.anchor: بناء على أن فعل المضاعف إذا لم يكن للتعدية كان المقصود منه الدلالة على التكثير من المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Figurative intensification can treat intellectual labor—finding subtle meanings and choosing exact expression—as extensive work.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون التكثير في ذلك مجازيا واعتباريا بأن ينزل كد الفكر في تحصيل المعاني الدقيقة

rows.speaker: صحار العبدي
rows.claim: Asked by Muawiya about eloquence, Ṣaḥār al-ʿAbdī said to speak without error and answer without delay, then jokingly asked to retract the demand to do both.
rows.anchor: كتفسير صحار العبدي وقد سأله معاوية عن البلاغة فقال : أن تقول فلا تخطئ ، وتجيب فلا تبطئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive sense of verbal explanation is supported by the Quran’s phrase أحسن تفسيرا in 25:33.
rows.anchor: ويشهد لهذا قوله تعالى ) ولا يأتونك بمثل إلا جئناك بالحق وأحسن تفسيرا (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether gemination intensifies a transitive verb is disputed; Ibn Ashur says a speaker may choose it over hamza to imply abundance by association with its intransitive use.
rows.anchor: فأما إذا كان فعل المضاعف للتعدية فإن إفادته التكثير مختلف فيها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: In the Kashshaf preface, al-Zamakhshari pairs أنزل and نزله to express gradual, repeated revelation, matching the intensive force of نزّل.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال العلامة الزمخشري في خطبة الكشاف الحمد لله الذي أنزل القرآن كلاما مؤلفا منظما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur says intensification from a transitive geminate is a pragmatic implication: choosing its heavier form over hamza signals abundance, reinforced by pairing both forms.
rows.anchor: وأنا أرى أن استفادة معنى التكثير في حال استعمال التضعيف للتعدية أمر من مستتبعات الكلام

rows.speaker: بعض مشايخ القرافي
rows.claim: A teacher cited by al-Qarafi distinguishes light فرق for meanings and doubled فرّق for bodies, reasoning that more letters convey greater or stronger meaning.
rows.anchor: وعزا شهاب الدين القرافي في أول أنواء البروق إلى بعض مشايخه أن العرب فرقوا بين فرق

rows.speaker: القرافي
rows.claim: Al-Qarafi objects that the light-versus-heavy distinction does not hold consistently.
rows.anchor: واستشكله هو بعدم اطراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects that distinction as rhetorical nicety rather than sound rule: the forms signal real or figurative abundance, not abstract meanings versus physical objects.
rows.anchor: بل هو أشبه باللطائف منه بالحقائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فرقناه in 17:106 is read with either a light or doubled consonant; 2:285 also uses the light form لا نفرق.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى ) وقرآنا فرقناه ( قرىء بالتشديد والتخفيف

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid’s line pairs the verb قدم with its noun إقدام, illustrating alternation between related verb forms.
rows.anchor: وقال لبيد : فمضى وقدمها وكانت عادة منه إذا هي عردت إقدامها

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says فعل and أفعل alternate; the proposed distinction concerns the verb’s meaning, not whether its object is a body.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه إن فعل وأفعل يتعاقبان على أن التفرقة عند مثبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In technical usage, tafsir is the discipline that explains Quranic words and meanings derived from them, briefly or at length.
rows.anchor: والتفسير في الاصطلاح نقول : هو اسم للعلم الباحث عن بيان معاني ألفاظ القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relation between lexical and technical senses of tafsir needs little explanation.
rows.anchor: والمناسبة بين المعنى الأصلي والمعنى المنقول إليه لا يحتاج إلى تطويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir’s subject is Quranic wording as examined for meaning and inference.
rows.anchor: وموضوع التفسير : ألفاظ القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir differs from qira’at because disciplines are distinguished by their subjects and the aspects from which they examine them.
rows.anchor: وبهذه الحيثية خالف علم القراءات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling tafsir a science is loose: knowledge may mean cognition, the rational faculty, certain belief, or demonstrable universal propositions, none of which describes tafsir’s material.
rows.anchor: هذا وفي عد التفسير علما تسامح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir usually treats particular concepts, not provable universal propositions: explaining words is verbal definition, while derivation proceeds by entailment.
rows.anchor: فأما تفسير الألفاظ فهو من قبيل التعريف اللفظي
